Nanni Si Lehed Shaam Ke Zindaan Main Bana Ke,

Maa Laut Ke Jaati Hai, Sakina Ko Sula Ke,

Ik Tasht Main Aaya Hai, Jo Saaman e Rihayi,

Abbas Ka Sar Bhi Hai, Sakina Ke Gohar Bhi,

Sar Rakhay Kahan Dur Kahan Maa Rakhay Chupa Ke,

Rassi Se Jakarte Huway, Kharoun Pe Chala Te,

Har Roz Sazayen Nayi, Uss Bachi Ko Detay,

Maani Bhi Samajhti Na Thi Jo Bachi Saza Ke,

Kal Tak Thi Jo Lori Wohi, Ab Hogaya Noha,

Un Baatoun Ko Jab Sochti, Dil Kat Tha Maa Ka,

Dil Beti Ka Behlati Thi Kal Tak Jo Suna Ke,

Abbas Ke Mashkeezay Ko, Naizay Pe Uthatay,

Baatain Kabhi Ghazi Ki, Shahadat Ki Sunatay,

Khush Hotay Rahay Shaami, Sakina Ko Sata Ke,

Akbar Jo Lehed Abid e Muztar Ne Banayi,

Woh Matti Bhi Turbat Main, Sakina Ki Milayi,

Thi Matti Jo Zindaan Main Kaam Aayi Rida Ke,

from pathlib import Path
import re
p=Path('src/data/lyrics/nanni-si-lehed-shaam-ke-zindaan-main-bana-ke-nw-ca54b63ce949.md')
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split('---\\n', 2)
roman=meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n',1)[1]
def counts(s):
    return [sum(not line.strip().isdigit() for line in block.splitlines()) for block in re.split(r'\\n\\s*\\n',s.strip())]
assert counts(roman)==counts(body)==[2,3,3,3,3,3]
print('Both editions contain 17 verses across the opening and five stanzas.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 17 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Verified that both versions have the same two-line opening and five numbered stanzas. Updated the title and right-to-left direction, and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

I read `dur` as `دُر` (pearl), consistent with `gohar` in the preceding verse, and `Kharoun` as `خروں` (donkeys).
